title: What to send before a pre-application meeting with a planner

text:
Topics: process, pre-application, variance

# What to send before a pre-application meeting with a planner

## Question

Can we schedule a meeting with a planner to review preliminary variance findings and plans before submitting?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> Please send preliminary drawings or schematics, variance findings, and any of your questions so we can assign you to the planner best suited for your project and prepare for the meeting.

title: No alterations to portions of a building over the property line; in-kind repairs allowed
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-20
text:
Topics: property line, encroachment, alterations, repairs

# No alterations to portions of a building over the property line; in-kind repairs allowed

## Question

The survey shows the house's northern side is over the property line. What are the implications for alterations?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> Unfortunately there are no options for alterations to portions of the building existing over the property line, however, in-kind repairs would be allowed.

## Context

Answered after Planning and Building and Public Works conferred. Likely applies generally to encroaching structures; confirm before relying on it for another property.

title: FAR, lot coverage and landscape coverage include the entire footprint, even past the property line
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-26
text:
Topics: floor area ratio, FAR, lot coverage, landscape coverage, measurement, property line

# FAR, lot coverage and landscape coverage include the entire footprint, even past the property line

## Question

The zoning ordinance has no guidance on floor area, lot coverage or FAR for structures encroaching onto another property. We propose calculating lot coverage and FAR excluding any portion over the property line. Should these values be calculated differently?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> To clarify, the entire footprint (of all structures) and floor area of the habitable spaces must be included when calculating FAR, lot coverage, and landscape coverage, regardless of location—even for portions that extend beyond the property boundaries.

## Context

The applicant proposed excluding the portion over the property line, per the definitions in 17.90.020. Staff ruled the opposite. Staff also pointed to a chapter of the Design Guidelines (chapter not named in the email).

title: Interior changes allowed in a portion over the property line if the exterior is unaffected
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-26
text:
Topics: interior, property line, alterations

# Interior changes allowed in a portion over the property line if the exterior is unaffected

## Question

Does the restriction on alterations include work on the interior of the building?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> No, we would still allow changes to the interior as long as the exterior is unaffected.

title: No roof changes for the portion of a structure past the property line
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-26
text:
Topics: roof, property line, garage, alterations

# No roof changes for the portion of a structure past the property line

## Question

Can the roof be modified where the structure extends past the property boundary?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> Also, no roof changes will be allowed for portion extending past the property boundary.

## Context

Repeated on 2026-10-28 for the garage: "The roof would not be allowed to be modified for the portion of the garage that is built over the property line."

title: Replacing a window with another is allowed if size, location, operation, recess and lite pattern don't change
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-26
text:
Topics: windows, double pane, replacement, property line

# Replacing a window with another is allowed if size, location, operation, recess and lite pattern don't change

## Question

Can the windows over the property line be replaced with new double-pane windows if they are the same size, or do we have to keep the old single-pane windows?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> You could replace the window with another provided that there is no change in the following: The size or location of the window. The operation of the window. The recess of the window measured from exterior wall face to the window sash. The divided lite pattern (if any), provided that any new divided lites are either true divided lites or 3-dimensional simulated divided lites.

## Context

Asked about windows over the property line; the criteria match the city's Window Replacement Policy.

title: Show a side setback over the property line as a negative value with a note
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-26
text:

# Show a side setback over the property line as a negative value with a note

## Question

Should the side setback where the house is over the property line be expressed as a negative value, or should it be 0?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> A negative value with a note indicating the encroachment would be fine.

title: A smaller window in an existing opening over the property line is not an in-kind repair
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-26
text:
Topics: windows, property line, in-kind repair

# A smaller window in an existing opening over the property line is not an in-kind repair

## Question

In-kind repairs are allowed for portions of the building over the property line. Would this allow replacing an existing window with a smaller window within the existing opening?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> No, this change would not constitute an in-kind repair.

title: A structure over the property line could not be converted to habitable space
cite: Piedmont Planning staff, Assistant Planner, written answer 2026-10-29
text:
Topics: ADU, garage conversion, property line, habitable space

# A structure over the property line could not be converted to habitable space

## Question

If converting the existing garage (partly over the property line) to an ADU, can the roof be raised, up to 18 feet, with a loft?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> Unfortunately, a structure situated over the property line could not be converted to habitable space. If the owners wanted to develop an ADU on the property, they could not convert the existing garage.

# Staff see a path forward for the garage-to-ADU conversion (details pending)

## Question

Given a likely original surveying error, can the garage be converted to an ADU (by correcting the line, rebuilding shifted, or building a new wall inside the encroaching one)?

## Staff answer (verbatim)

> I've have looked into your inquiry with the team and believe there is a path forward for the garage to ADU conversion.

## Context

Followed the applicant's Nov 2 email: the 1951 survey likely mis-located the line; options raised were correcting deeds and easement, rebuilding the garage shifted onto the lot, or a new inner wall. Details to be discussed at a meeting on 2026-11-09. Update this record with what staff say there.
